# <span id="aanchor27"></span> Volume Editor Grid Tab Details

[&lt;&lt; Back](Volume%20Editor.md#Tabs) \| <a href="#" class="selected">Batch</a> \| [Periodic](Periodic%20Tab.md) \| [Daily](Daily%20Tab.md) \| [Monthly](Monthly%20Tab.md) \| [Alternate Periodic](Alternate%20Periodic%20Tab.md)

#### Batch Tab

This tab is only available for liquid meters.

The Volume Editor Batch tab shows the volume of liquid product passed through a meter over a specific period of time. Data can be edited at the batch level for Characteristics, Analysis, and Flow Data. If there is no batch present for the time frame specified, a batch will be created. Once a batch is created, editing the Start and End Date on batches is prohibited. You must split the batch in order to alter the dates.

If the edited batch time frame overlaps the time frame for a batch that is imported later, that batch will not be imported.

When editing a batch record, you can easily see on the Flow Data tab whether a batch exists. If there is not an existing batch for the time frame, a "V" (virtual batch) will display in the columns next to the start date. There is not an indicator on the other tabs such as Characteristic or Analysis.

By default, the batch total record is calculated from the sum of the periodic records within the batch.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 618;height: 406;" />

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Menu Options">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Right-Click Menu Options</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Menu Options">

The following options are available on the Batch tab:

- **Span Edit** – Allows you to edit multiple records at once.
  - **Purge** – Opens the Meter Purge screen with the meter and selected month pre-populated.
    <div class="procedure">

    To initiate a meter purge:

    1.  Modify the selections or proceed with the pre-populated selections.
    2.  Click the **Purge** button.

    When the purge is complete, the Volume Editor will refresh.

    Accessing this feature requires **Purge** privileges.

    </div>
  - **Edit to Original** – Edit data to the original values.
    <div>

    The Edit to Original function re-imports the original (revision 0) data of a record. This new import then contains the same data as revision 0. This allows users to edit the original data as if it were imported, saving all prior revisions as an audit trail.

    If revision 0 exists, and the current revision is greater than 0, the Edit to Original process will complete. If a record within the selected range cannot be edited back to original, a pop-up will display, indicating that there were records that could not be edited to the original data, and the dates of those records will display in red. That color will reset if the Volume Editor grid is refreshed.

    This option is not available for line pack meters.

    <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Process Logic">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Process Logic</a>

    <div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Process Logic">

    FLOWCAL adheres to the following conventions when users choose to edit to original data:

    - If a user chooses to edit to original, and the meter or ticket contains *only* an original (revision 0) record, no action will be taken for that record. This will not be considered a failure or included in the list of tickets that could not be updated.
    - For liquid meters:
      - If a user chooses to edit to original on the Batch tab, the revision 0 batch (if it exists) will be promoted to current and will be allocated to the underlying periodic records. This is independent of whether the data is master, batch, or periodic.
      - If a user chooses to edit to original on the Periodic tab, the revision 0 batch (if it exists) will be promoted to current. The batch will be recalculated from the underlying periodics. This is independent of whether the data is master, batch, or periodic.

    </div>

    </div>
- **Batch**
  - **Prove Adjustment** – Used when manually creating a prove adjustment on a batch to adjust prior and current adjustments for meter factor, K-factor, and density meter factor values.

    This option is not available for line pack meters.

  - **Ticket** – Prints the meter batch ticket for the selected batch. If multiple batches are selected, this option is disabled. Because reports run off data saved in the database, this menu option is disabled if you have any unsaved changes.

  - **Ticket with Internal Notes** – Prints the Meter Batch Ticket report and includes notes that are marked as internal.

  - **Split - Simple** – When this option is selected, you can select a batch and specify where in the batch the split should occur. Two batches are then created from that single batch (i.e., a simplistic batch split). The two new batches are calculated from the sum of the original periodic records that fall within each batch time frame.

    The screen that comes up for this option has two modes: Slider Entry and Free-Form Entry. When you edit using the Free-Form Entry option, you must also select if the data should be allocated "pro-rata" or "straight line". For both cases, the batch number for the second batch can be manually entered. This functionality is available for meters with both daily and hourly data.

    This option is available when a single batch is selected.

  - **Split - Advanced** – Allows you to perform a more advanced batch splitting action. When this option is selected, you can edit any flowing parameters, as well as meter factor and DMF, on the new batch. First, edit the left side of the batch, choosing the date of the split. After completing the edit of the first batch, enter data for the second batch. You'll have the option of doing "pro-rata" or "straight line" data allocation upon saving.

    This option is available when a single batch is selected, and you have saved pending edits. This option is not available for line pack meters.

  - **Split - Periodic** – When this option is selected, you'll first specify the date and time for the batch split, and then specify flowing parameters, such as mass, GSV and NSV, for each portion of the record being split. After these values are specified, new batch totals are calculated from the split periodic records and the other periodic records that fall within the batch time frames.

    This option is not available for line pack meters.

  - **Merge** – This option joins two batches. The resulting batch will have the same batch number as the batch with the earliest time stamp before the split.

    This option is available when two adjacent batches with the same product are selected.

  - **Sample Override** – Allows you to select either a standalone sample or a sample from a quality source as the sample to be used for the selected batches. The product on the first of the selected batches is used to determine which samples are valid. If a quality source is assigned to the meter, the override sample is used on the batch instead of the quality sample. Once the sample override is applied, any updates to the sample are applied to the batch by the GQ Apply service. Different samples can be selected as override samples at different times if desired. Only samples with a product that matches the product on the batch, or that do not have a product can be selected. When applied, a volume recalculation is performed using the correlation factor. (See: [Recalculation Methods](Recalculation%20Methods.md))
- **Quick Sum** – When this option is enabled, the monthly sum quick view is replaced to display the sum or average of selected rows in the Volume Editor.
- **Monthly Sum** – When this option is enabled, a quick view of the monthly sum is displayed at the bottom of the Volume Editor screen.
- **Add Note** – Allows you to add notes to any record in the Volume Editor.
- **View Notes** – Allows you to view notes for any record in the Volume Editor.
- **Prove Reports** – When a PFX file is imported, it can contain a PDF of the prove report. (This option is not available for line pack meters.)
  - If the prove report is imported into FLOWCAL via PFX file, the report will be available under Reports \> Prove Reports. An "R" will display in the character column next to the batch to which the prove report is applied, and the MF will be updated accordingly

  - If the prove report is imported through TESTit, the report will be available under Reports \> Test Reports. An "R" will display in the character column next to the batch to which the prove report is applied, but the MF will *not* be updated.

    Prove reports imported through TESTit will not trigger Master Characteristic validations.
- **Edit Columns** – Allows a you to change the columns displayed in the Volume Editor.
- **Accept ACBI** – If periodic data that does not already have batches is imported, FLOWCAL will create an <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCTextPopup MCTextPopupHotSpot MCTextPopup_Open glossaryTerm MCTextPopupHotSpot_" alt="Closed" data-mc-alt2="Open">ACBI<span class="MCTextPopupBody popupBody"><span class="MCTextPopupArrow"></span>Automatically Created Batch Upon Import</span></a> on the batch tab in the Volume Editor. The Accept ACBI option is visible when you select a highlighted row in the Volume Editor that is an ACBI. When you accept an ACBI batch:
  - The most current revision of the batch will no longer show as “ACBI” (the original revision will still show as “ACBI”)

  - An edit reason of "ACBI Batch accepted" will be applied to that revision.

  - The revision number will be incremented.

  - All future edits will increment the batch revision; with ACBI batches, revision will always remain revision 1.

    

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 351;height: 255;" />

</div>

All of the flow data for the selected batch is viewable from the Flow Data tab. The **From** and **To** dates at the top show the beginning and end times for the selected batch.

##### Custom Fields



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 539;height: 383;" />

There are 20 batch-specific custom fields that can be imported into FLOWCAL via CFX, text field, or Transaction Queue import.

##### Accounting



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 541;height: 361;" />

The Accounting tab allows the user to set the following options:

- **Shipper/Outside Shipper** – A company that is sending the product. Company must already exist and be specified as a shipper in Company Manager
- **From/To Facility** – Used to track inventory. Facility must be previously defined under Settings Manager \> Liquids \> Facilities
- **Customer Ticket ID** – Unique identification of batch provided by customer.
- **Witness** – Name of purchaser’s representative. Must be a previously defined contact under Contact Manager
- **Operator** – Name of operating company. Name must be previously defined in Company Manager.
- **Seal 1 Off/On** – Values that must match the previous and successive batches associated with the meter
- **Seal 2 Off/On** - Values that must match the previous and successive batches associated with the meter

##### Components



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 544;height: 467;" />

Component level data for the select batch can be viewed here. Values will display in units specified under the **Meter Characteristic** \> **Units tab** \> **Component Volume**.
